hook.text: Amazon paid no federal income tax on $11 billion profit in 2018. How? Past losses.

buildup.text: When a business loses money one year, it can use that loss to offset future profits.

discovery.text: This is a 'net operating loss carryforward'—it reduces taxable income in profitable years.

twist.text: Companies that invested heavily for years can shelter enormous profits when they finally succeed.

climax.text: The rule encourages risk-taking—but critics say billion-dollar companies shouldn't pay zero tax.

punchline.text: Yesterday's losses become today's tax savings.

quiz.question: What is a tax loss carryforward?
options: Using past losses to offset future taxable profit
Moving tax payments to the next year
Carrying tax refunds to other businesses

details.summary: Tax loss carryforwards allow businesses to use losses from one year to reduce taxable income in future profitable years, preventing companies from being taxed on long-term breakeven results just because profits and losses fall in different years.
details.whyItMatters: Loss carryforwards are a critical tax planning mechanism that ensures businesses are taxed on their economic reality over time, not penalized by the arbitrary boundaries of calendar years.
takeaways: Net operating losses from unprofitable years can be carried forward to offset future taxable income
This prevents businesses from being taxed unfairly when losses and profits occur in different years
U.S. tax law limits carryforward deductions to 80% of taxable income in any given year

faq.question: What is a tax loss carryforward?
faq.answer: When a business loses money in a year, it can carry that loss forward to offset taxable income in future profitable years. If a company loses $500,000 this year and earns $700,000 next year, it can apply the loss against future income, reducing next year's taxable amount to $200,000.

faq.question: Why do loss carryforwards exist?
faq.answer: Without them, a business that loses $1 million in year one and earns $1 million in year two would pay full tax on year two's profit despite breaking even overall. Carryforwards ensure businesses are taxed on their real economic performance over time, not penalized by calendar boundaries.
